release_notes_draft: Microwave Orbit release (internal variant: orbit-quant-v2) - draft. Summary: Deploys an optimized quantized variant of the inference runtime with attention kernel improvements and KV prewarm support. Expected benefits: 15-25% token-cost reduction on long-context workloads, ~10% median latency improvement on dedicated pools. Compatibility: API unchanged; response schema preserved. Known limitations: occasional cold-starts affecting first 2 requests per VM (workaround: prewarm on heavy routes). Rollout plan: staged canary over 24h with automated rollback gates. Action items for customers: none unless you pin model variants; reach out to solutions-eng if you require immediate opt-out. Contact: ops@redwood.ai for incidents.
content:
Purpose:
This note collects the quick-operational checklist, the hour-by-hour microwave 'orbit' rollout cadence, and a short draft of release notes for the orbit quantized runtime. Intended audience: release engineer on-shift, SREs, on-call infra, and DE owners for the affected routes.

Scope and constraints:
- Targets the hosted API and dedicated pools in us-west1 and eu-west1. Private/VPC will be scheduled separately (see linked artifact).
- This is a performance/efficiency roll with zero contract API changes. Primary risk: perf regressions at scale due to batching heuristics and new kernel selection.

Key monitoring signals (watchlist):
- Latency p50/p90/p99 by route and model variant
- Error rate (5xx + runtime timeouts) per minute
- KV-cache hit ratio and cold-caused misses
- GPU memory pressure and OOM events on dedicated nodes
- Token-per-request delta vs baseline and batch utilization metrics

Circuit breakers and gate thresholds (operational):
- Immediate rollback if error-rate > 1% sustained for 5m on canary
- Pause expansion if p90 increases > 25% vs baseline and stays for 10m
- Throttle if GPU mem > 85% and OOMs observed
- Fallback to older variant automatically if model inference latency breaches hard SLO (300ms p90)

Runbook highlights and quick commands:
- Check current image: gcloud artifacts docker images list --repository=... --filter="abc1234"
- Trigger canary: tools/deploy --route model-routing/orbit --percent=1 --tag orbit-2026-09
- Rollback: tools/rollout rollback --route model-routing/orbit --to-tag orbit-prev-2026-08 (test rollback-id rb-2026-09-10-1 before live)

Unresolved questions / TODOs:
- Confirm whether quant-v2 needs a special kv-cache prewarm size parameter (asked infra: @Marcus Li).
- Decide on noisy-alert suppression window length (2h proposed) — SRE to confirm.
- Verify whether dedicated autoscaler will spin up extra VMs under steady 60% traffic split (note: observed delayed scaling in canary-emu last week).

Quick notes to on-shift engineer:
- Start with the dry-run checklist; do not skip staging smoke. Record the smoke run id in the Slack thread.
- On canary expand decisions, post short summary in #deploy-ops and tag product owners.
- If rollback is needed, prefer fast rollback (blue->green) over staging pause unless we see widespread non-deterministic failures.

Field-ops annotations (things we learned during rehearsal):
- Sampling at 100% for the first 10 minutes gave good traces but overloaded the trace-collector; keep heavy sampling to 15m max and point to a short retention bucket.
- Synthetic prompts used for smoke need to include long-context tokens (>1024) to surface batch kernel regressions.
- Automated fallback worked in 2/3 test cases, one edge-case failed due to input shape mismatch (PR link included).

Appendix - quick links and references:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/598
- Dry-run traces: gs://redwood-dryruns/orbit/2026-09-10/trace-01
- JIRA: ENG-1423 (kernel selection tuning), OPS-987 (canary autoscaler investigation)
- Slack: #deploy-ops (bookmark thread pinned)

End of notes. Keep this doc as the single source for the operator during the 2026-09-10 window; move final release notes to ops-release-notes when rollout completes.
